title: Billy May's Lunceford tribute record
summary: Billy May transcribed the Lunceford arrangements and Joe Thomas praised him.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: I made that tribute to Lunceford with Billy May. Billy May transcribed all the arrangements off the records, note for note. Perfect. And when we got to the record date, Joe Thomas was there -- we had sent for some guys. You know, they got Willie and they got Joe...
Trummy. And Gerald was in town; I don't know why they didn't get him. He wasn't on the date.

Yeah. Anyway, Joe Thomas said, "Who wrote these arrangements? They're perfect." And Billy was lookin' at him; you know, he was still juicin' -- and he says, "I did. And it wasn't easy." And Joe Thomas says, "Well, you just went through a whole bunch of trouble. I got the whole book in my basement. You could have called me up, I'd have mailed it out, and that would be the end of it." He didn't have to do it. But he said, "You did a
masterful job, because you didn't make one mistake." Of course, Billy got paid for it.
But it's not easy, figuring out all those intricate voicings.
